text: Tatiana Zatulovskaya (Hebrew: טטיאנה זטולובסקיה; Russian: Татьяна Яковлевна Затуловская, Tatiana Yakovlevna Zatulovskaya; 8 December 1935 – 2 July 2017) was an Israeli chess player of Soviet and Russian origin. She earned three titles as a Soviet women's champion, winning the Women's Soviet Chess Championship in 1960, 1962, and 1963. She represented the USSR at the Women's Chess Olympiad in 1963 and 1966, securing team gold medals on both occasions, and won an individual silver medal in 1963 and an individual gold in 1966. During the 1960s and 1970s, she frequently qualified for Interzonals and Candidates Tournaments for the Women's World Chess Championship. In 1993, she won the Women's Seniors World Championship with a score of 10 out of 11 points (10 wins, 0 losses, and 2 draws), and repeated this victory in 1997. In 2000, she emigrated to Israel, where she represented the country at the 2002 Women's Chess Olympiad. She was awarded the title of Woman International Master (WIM) in 1961 and Woman Grandmaster (WGM) in 1976 by FIDE. Her last name may also be spelled as Zatulovskaia or Zatulovskaja. Zatulovskaya died on 2 July 2017 at the age of 81. In her lifetime, she was also a geological engineer and a good gymnast.
